Guidance & outlook: The underlying trends are encouraging, with annualised RoA improving to 0.45% in Q4 FY26, compared to 0.17% for FY26 as a whole.
The share of average retail deposits as per LCR improved to 47.9% in Q4 FY2026 vs 46.6% in Q4 FY2025.
The cost of fund improved 5.14% in Q4FY2026 vs 5.6% in Q4 FY2025.
Growth & demand: The IMF projects global growth of 3.1% in 2026, lower than earlier estimates, while inflation is expected to remain elevated.
Despite these headwinds, India stood out as a resilient long-term growth story, with real GDP growth of 7.7% supported by strong domestic demand and private consumption.

Integrated Annual Report 2025-26 DIGITAL PAYMENTS MOVED TO MAINSTREAM INFRASTRUCTURE ESG REGULATION MOVED FROM VOLUNTARY TO STRUCTURAL UPI processed over 24,162 crore transactions in FY2026, representing an almost 12,000-fold surge in volume since its launch in FY2017.
Margins & costs: Bank credit grew 16% year-on-year as of March 31, 2026, supported by benign CPI inflation, lower policy rates, and ample liquidity.
The Bank reported a consolidated pre-provision operating profit of ₹9,180 crore and a Profit After Tax of ₹889 crore for FY2025-26.

POISED FOR GROWTH IN A RECALIBRATING LANDSCAPE Integrated Annual Report 2025-26 Corporate OverviewIntegrated Annual Report 2025-26 A SUPPORTIVE MONETARY CYCLE IMPROVED TRANSMISSION AND MARGINS The RBI delivered a cumulative 125 basis points of rate cuts through FY2026, bringing the repo rate down to 5.25% by December 2025, in a decisive shift from its earlie…
Capex & expansion: Strong domestic demand, coupled with the Government's sustained infrastructure push, with budgeted capital expenditure of over ₹12 Lakh crore, further reinforces this outlook.

The share of retail deposits improved to 47.9% from 46.6% in the previous financial year, supported by robust, new-to-bank CASA acquisitions and healthy growth across our NRI and Affluent Banking franchise.

We also continued to diversify our rural franchise, with our merchant loan book growing 11% year-on-year to over 570K merchant borrowers, and our affordable housing portfolio growing 24% year-on-year, alongside expansion in Kisan Credit and other rural lending segments, positioning the business for more stable and sustainable growth.
Balance sheet & cash: To declare dividend at the rate of ₹1.50 per equity share of ₹10 each of the Bank, fully paid, for the Financial Year ended March 31, 2026.
Microfinance The rural banking franchise continued to leverage its deep distribution network across ~1.62 Lakh villages in 21 states.
Development Finance Tie-Ups Refinancing from development institutions constituted 58% of the Bank's borrowing mix during FY2026, supporting diversified funding sources.
Risks & challenges: While downside risks to growth and upside risks to inflation remain, India's strong domestic fundamentals and continued policy support position the economy well to navigate an uncertain global environment.

Our loan book stood at ₹3.15 Lakh crore year-on-year as the Bank pursued balance sheet optimisation by shedding inefficient assets, growing core retail assets, and adopting a risk-adjusted approach to allocation of capital for growth.
Notably, 100% of Board members attended training during the year, covering IT and cybersecurity, corporate governance, risk management, and ESG.
